In the Go repo at /opt/gsb-fleet/workspaces/inst-15/A/task045, I'm adding a recovery rule: when replaying queue.log, every success record (logEntry with T="result" or T="state" and Status="success", i.e. Go `kindResult`/`kindState` + `StatusSuccess`, typically carrying ConsumeFrom/ConsumeTo/ConsumeNonce/ConsumeBy or legacy ConsumeKey) must have a TRUSTED header entry (kindHeader, Trusted=true) for the SAME source chain (the submit entry's "from" / success entry's "consumeFrom") with Height >= the message's proofAt height, and that header must appear in the log BEFORE the success result entry (for kindResult); for kindState (compacted snapshot) the snapshot retains headers so any header in the compacted log counts.

I need you to audit ALL *_test.go files under /opt/gsb-fleet/workspaces/inst-15/A/task045 (both relayproof/ and cmd/relayproof/) for HAND-CRAFTED log fixtures (logEntry structs written via writeLegacyLog or similar direct log writers, or manually-edited raw bytes) that contain a success record WITHOUT such a covering trusted header before it. Fixtures produced via the real Queue API (RegisterSource/UpsertHeader/Submit/Advance) are always legal and don't matter — only hand-built logEntry lists / raw byte manipulations.

For each such fixture, report:
1. File path and test/helper function name (with line numbers).
2. The success message id, source chain, proof-at height.
3. What header entries (if any) precede it in that fixture: chain/height/trusted.
4. Whether the test expects Open to SUCCEED or fail (and with what error), since fixtures that already expect ErrCorrupt are fine.

Pay special attention to: relayproof/recovery_time_test.go, relayproof/store_from_bytes_test.go, relayproof/store_to_bytes_test.go, relayproof/store_head_test.go, relayproof/store_save_parity_test.go, relayproof/store_id_bytes_test.go, relayproof/store_payload_bytes_test.go, relayproof/paths_test.go, cmd/relayproof/*_test.go, and any helper that builds generic "valid log" entry lists reused by many tests.

List every helper that constructs reusable log entry lists (e.g. base-log helpers) and state whether their success records have covering trusted headers. Be thorough and report exact findings concisely; do not modify anything.

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

1	package main
2	
3	// End-to-end behaviour when a state directory's queue.log records a waiting
4	// result and then a success stamped before that message's scheduled retry.
5	// The record is complete and checksum-valid, and every other recovery rule
6	// passes, but no normal advance could have delivered the message — and
7	// consumed its nonce — while the backoff was still running. Opening the
8	// directory must fail with the corrupt exit code 12, print no query records
9	// (including none for an unrelated, fully valid message earlier in the log),
10	// explain the retry-timing violation on stderr, and leave queue.log
11	// byte-for-byte untouched.
12	
13	import (
14		"os"
15		"path/filepath"
16		"strings"
17		"testing"
18	)
19	
20	// cliEarlySuccessLog is a valid version record followed by: a registered
21	// source with a covering trusted header, a fully delivered message m0, and
22	// message w which waits at 1000ms (retry scheduled for 2000ms) but is then
23	// recorded successful at 1500ms — before its backoff elapsed.
24	func cliEarlySuccessLog() []byte {
25		var raw []byte
26		raw = append(raw, cliLogMagic...)
27		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(`{"t":"version","v":1}`))...)
28		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(`{"t":"source","chain":"a"}`))...)
29		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(
30			`{"t":"header","chain":"a","height":100,"root":"0x100","trusted":true}`))...)
31		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(
32			`{"t":"submit","seq":0,"id":"m0","from":"a","to":"b","nonce":1,"proofAt":10}`))...)
33		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(
34			`{"t":"result","now":500,"id":"m0","status":"success",`+
35				`"reason":"delivered; proof verified by trusted header at height 100","attempts":1,`+
36				`"consumeFrom":"a","consumeTo":"b","consumeNonce":1,"consumeBy":"m0"}`))...)
37		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(
38			`{"t":"submit","seq":1,"id":"w","from":"a","to":"b","nonce":7,"proofAt":10}`))...)
39		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(
40			`{"t":"result","now":1000,"id":"w","status":"waiting",`+
41				`"reason":"waiting for trusted header covering height 10 (current 100)","attempts":1,"nextRetry":2000}`))...)
42		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(
43			`{"t":"result","now":1500,"id":"w","status":"success",`+
44				`"reason":"delivered; proof verified by trusted header at height 100","attempts":2,`+
45				`"consumeFrom":"a","consumeTo":"b","consumeNonce":7,"consumeBy":"w"}`))...)
46		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(`{"t":"advance","now":1500}`))...)
47		return raw
48	}
49	
50	// A pre-retry success rejects the whole directory on open: exit code 12, no
51	// query output at all — the valid m0 record must not be partially served —
52	// the error names the scheduling violation, and a repeated open keeps failing
53	// without rewriting the log.
54	func TestCLIQueryEarlySuccessDuringBackoffCorruptExit12(t *testing.T) {
55		state := t.TempDir()
56		raw := cliEarlySuccessLog()
57		writeCLIStateLog(t, state, raw)
58	
59		check := func(r cliResult) {
60			t.Helper()
61			if r.code != 12 {
62				t.Fatalf("want corrupt exit code 12, got %d (stdout=%q stderr=%q)", r.code, r.stdout, r.stderr)
63			}
64			if r.stdout != "" {
65				t.Fatalf("a corrupt directory must print no query records: %q", r.stdout)
66			}
67			for _, want := range []string{"corrupt", "precedes scheduled retry 2000", `"w"`} {
68				if !strings.Contains(r.stderr, want) {
69					t.Fatalf("stderr missing %q:\n%s", want, r.stderr)
70				}
71			}
72			got, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(state, "queue.log"))
73			if err != nil {
74				t.Fatal(err)
75			}
76			if string(got) != string(raw) {
77				t.Fatalf("queue.log changed on rejected open: want %d bytes, got %d bytes", len(raw), len(got))
78			}
79		}
80	
81		check(queueCLI(t, state, "query"))
82		check(queueCLI(t, state, "query", "--id", "m0"))
83		check(queueCLI(t, state, "advance", "--now", "3000"))
84	
85		// The bytes survive a second rejected open as well.
86		check(queueCLI(t, state, "query"))
87	}

1	package main
2	
3	// End-to-end behaviour when an existing state directory's queue.log carries
4	// a complete, checksum-valid header record that names BOTH root forms. Such a
5	// record is on-disk corruption (ErrCorrupt), not the live ErrHeaderConflict a
6	// user gets for same-height/different-root saves: opening the directory must
7	// fail with the corrupt exit code 12, say plainly that the header root carried
8	// both representations, print no query results, and leave queue.log
9	// byte-for-byte untouched — even when the offending record is the final frame
10	// (a complete record is never treated as a torn tail).
11	
12	import (
13		"encoding/binary"
14		"hash/crc32"
15		"os"
16		"path/filepath"
17		"strings"
18		"testing"
19	)
20	
21	const cliLogMagic = "RELAYPROOF-QUEUE-V1\n"
22	
23	// cliFrame wraps a JSON payload exactly as the queue log stores records:
24	// uint32-be length, payload, uint32-be CRC32-IEEE.
25	func cliFrame(payload []byte) []byte {
26		frame := make([]byte, 0, 4+len(payload)+4)
27		var hdr [4]byte
28		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(hdr[:], uint32(len(payload)))
29		frame = append(frame, hdr[:]...)
30		frame = append(frame, payload...)
31		var crc [4]byte
32		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(crc[:], crc32.ChecksumIEEE(payload))
33		frame = append(frame, crc[:]...)
34		return frame
35	}
36	
37	// cliLogWithCorruptHeader builds the smallest corrupt log: a valid leading
38	// version record followed by one complete trusted header naming both "root":""
39	// and a rootB64 that decodes to byte 0xFF — the exact gap the fix closes.
40	func cliLogWithCorruptHeader() []byte {
41		var raw []byte
42		raw = append(raw, cliLogMagic...)
43		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(`{"t":"version","v":1}`))...)
44		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(
45			`{"t":"header","chain":"x","height":100,"trusted":true,"root":"","rootB64":"/w=="}`))...)
46		return raw
47	}
48	
49	func writeCLIStateLog(t *testing.T, state string, data []byte) {
50		t.Helper()
51		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(state, "queue.log"), data, 0o600); err != nil {
52			t.Fatal(err)
53		}
54	}
55	
56	// assertCorruptExit12 opens the directory via the given CLI result and pins
57	// the corruption surface: exit code 12 (never the 16 header-conflict code),
58	// no stdout query output, a stderr explanation that names the two root
59	// representations, and an unchanged queue.log.
60	func assertCorruptExit12(t *testing.T, r cliResult, state string, wantLog []byte) {
61		t.Helper()
62		if r.code != 12 {
63			t.Fatalf("want corrupt exit code 12, got %d (stdout=%q stderr=%q)", r.code, r.stdout, r.stderr)
64		}
65		if r.stdout != "" {
66			t.Fatalf("a corrupt directory must print no query results: %q", r.stdout)
67		}
68		for _, want := range []string{"corrupt", "both root and rootB64"} {
69			if !strings.Contains(r.stderr, want) {
70				t.Fatalf("stderr missing %q:\n%s", want, r.stderr)
71			}
72		}
73		if strings.Contains(r.stderr, "trusted header conflict") {
74			t.Fatalf("on-disk dual-root corruption must not be reported as a live header conflict:\n%s", r.stderr)
75		}
76		got, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(state, "queue.log"))
77		if err != nil {
78			t.Fatal(err)
79		}
80		if string(got) != string(wantLog) {
81			t.Fatalf("queue.log changed on rejected open: want %d bytes, got %d bytes", len(wantLog), len(got))
82		}
83	}
84	
85	// A complete trusted header at the end of the log carrying both "root":"" and
86	// rootB64 rejects the directory on open: `queue query` (both the listing and a
87	// single-id lookup) exits 12 without output, names both root forms, and a
88	// repeated open keeps failing with the file untouched — it is never dropped as
89	// an unwritten torn tail.
90	func TestCLIQueryDualRootHeaderCorruptExit12(t *testing.T) {
91		state := t.TempDir()
92		raw := cliLogWithCorruptHeader()
93		writeCLIStateLog(t, state, raw)
94	
95		assertCorruptExit12(t, queueCLI(t, state, "query"), state, raw)
96	
97		// Single-id lookup opens the same directory and must fail identically.
98		assertCorruptExit12(t, queueCLI(t, state, "query", "--id", "anything"), state, raw)
99	
100		// The directory stays unopenable and byte-identical on a further attempt.
101		assertCorruptExit12(t, queueCLI(t, state, "query"), state, raw)
102	}
103	
104	// The dual-root record is corruption even when perfectly good records precede
105	// it: the listing must surface none of the normal messages already stored,
106	// proving the whole open is refused rather than partially served.
107	func TestCLIQueryDualRootHeaderHidesNormalResults(t *testing.T) {
108		state := t.TempDir()
109	
110		// Lay down normal, accepted state through the real CLI: a registered
111		// source, a trusted header covering height 90, and a deliverable message.
112		registerSource(t, state, "x")
113		if r := storeHeader(t, state, "x", 100, "0xaaa", true); r.code != 0 {
114			t.Fatalf("store initial header: %v", r)
115		}
116		submitMsg(t, state, "m1", "x", "y", 1, 90)
117	
118		// Append the corrupt dual-root header as the final, complete frame.
119		path := filepath.Join(state, "queue.log")
120		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
121		if err != nil {
122			t.Fatal(err)
123		}
124		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(
125			`{"t":"header","chain":"x","height":200,"trusted":true,"root":"","rootB64":"/w=="}`))...)
126		writeCLIStateLog(t, state, raw)
127	
128		r := queueCLI(t, state, "query")
129		assertCorruptExit12(t, r, state, raw)
130		if strings.Contains(r.stdout, "m1") {
131			t.Fatalf("normal message must not be served from a corrupt directory: %q", r.stdout)
132		}
133	}

16		"strings"
17		"testing"
18	)

21	// 2^32-1 byte body but carries almost nothing after the length header.
22	func cliLogWithHugeVersionLength() []byte {
23		var raw []byte
24		raw = append(raw, cliLogMagic...)
25		var hdr [4]byte
26		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(hdr[:], 0xFFFFFFFF)
27		raw = append(raw, hdr[:]...)
28		raw = append(raw, '{')
29		return raw

10	// Recovery must make every recorded success — an incrementally saved plain
11	// result and a compacted success state alike — satisfy the same delivery
12	// precondition a live advance applies: a trusted header of the message's own
13	// source chain, already saved (or retained by the snapshot), must cover its
14	// proof height. No header, only untrusted headers, or a highest trusted
15	// height below the proof height rejects the whole directory with ErrCorrupt,
16	// even when the record is complete, checksum-valid, well timed and carries a
17	// correct nonce attribution. A trusted height exactly equal to the proof
18	// height covers. The error names the message and the source chain and says
19	// the coverage is missing; the log keeps its exact length and bytes even when
20	// the bad record is the final frame.
21	
22	// coveringSuccessEntries is a complete legal log: source a with a trusted
23	// header at 100, message m proving at height 10, delivered at 1000.
24	func coveringSuccessEntries() []*logEntry {
25		return []*logEntry{
26			{T: kindSource, Chain: "a"},
27			{T: kindHeader, Chain: "a", Height: 100, Root: "0x100", Trusted: true},
28			{T: kindSubmit, Seq: 0, ID: "m", From: "a", To: "b", Nonce: 1, ProofAt: 10},
29			{T: kindResult, Now: 1000, ID: "m", Status: StatusSuccess,
30				Reason:   "delivered; proof verified by trusted header at height 100",
31				Attempts: 1, ConsumeFrom: "a", ConsumeTo: "b", ConsumeNonce: 1, ConsumeBy: "m"},
32			{T: kindAdvance, Now: 1000},
33		}
34	}
35	
36	func TestRecoveryRejectsSuccessWithoutCoverage(t *testing.T) {
37		t.Run("plain result with no header saved", func(t *testing.T) {
38			entries := []*logEntry{
39				{T: kindSource, Chain: "a"},
40				{T: kindSubmit, Seq: 0, ID: "m", From: "a", To: "b", Nonce: 1, ProofAt: 10},
41				// Complete, well-timed, correctly attributed — but no header entry
42				// exists anywhere in the log, and this is the final frame.
43				{T: kindResult, Now: 1000, ID: "m", Status: StatusSuccess,
44					Reason:   "delivered; proof verified by trusted header at height 100",
45					Attempts: 1, ConsumeFrom: "a", ConsumeTo: "b", ConsumeNonce: 1, ConsumeBy: "m"},
46			}
47			assertRecoveryCorrupt(t, entries, "success entry", `"m"`, `source chain "a"`,
48				"lacks trusted header coverage", "proof height 10", "no trusted header saved")
49		})
50	
51		t.Run("plain result with only a higher untrusted header", func(t *testing.T) {
52			entries := []*logEntry{
53				{T: kindSource, Chain: "a"},
54				{T: kindHeader, Chain: "a", Height: 500, Root: "0x500", Trusted: false},
55				{T: kindSubmit, Seq: 0, ID: "m", From: "a", To: "b", Nonce: 1, ProofAt: 101},
56				{T: kindResult, Now: 1000, ID: "m", Status: StatusSuccess,
57					Reason:   "delivered; proof verified by trusted header at height 500",
58					Attempts: 1, ConsumeFrom: "a", ConsumeTo: "b", ConsumeNonce: 1, ConsumeBy: "m"},

62		})

65			entries := []*logEntry{

17		"strings"
18		"testing"

22	// source with a trusted header at 100, the fully covered success m0 (proof
23	// 10), and message m1 whose success claims proof at 101 — above the highest
24	// trusted header — as the final frame.
25	func cliUncoveredSuccessLog() []byte {

27		raw = append(raw, cliLogMagic...)
28		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(`{"t":"version","v":1}`))...)

33			`{"t":"submit","seq":0,"id":"m0","from":"a","to":"b","nonce":1,"proofAt":10}`))...)

38		raw = append(raw, cliFrame([]byte(

One pre-existing "expects Open to succeed" fixture was already repaired in the working tree (`recovery_time_test.go`).

## Bottom line

After that one repair, every hand-crafted fixture whose success record expects `Open` to SUCCEED has a covering trusted header (same chain, `Height >= ProofAt`, earlier in the log for `kindResult`, present in the compacted log for `kindState`). Every uncovered hand-crafted success fixture already expects `ErrCorrupt` (exit 12 in the CLI) for another reason, or is a new dedicated coverage-rejection test. COVERED: header `a\x00b`@100 trusted at line 214 precedes the kindResult success at line 216 (legacy `ConsumeKey`). Used by `TestLegacyRawLogOpensDirectly` (expects Open success).
